name: Pennsylvania
agency: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT), Driver and Vehicle Services
permitAge: 16 (cannot apply before the 16th birthday); under 18 needs consent on DL-180TD from a parent, guardian, person in loco parentis or spouse 18 or older; knowledge test and vision screening (manual p. 1)

teen.supervisedHours: 65 hours, including at least 10 at night and 5 in bad weather; parent or guardian certifies on DL-180C (manual p. 2, 5)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months from the permit issue date before the road test (under 18) (manual p. 2)
teen.nightLimit: Junior license: no driving 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. unless with a parent, guardian, person in loco parentis or spouse 18 or older, or for employment, public or charitable service or a volunteer fire company (notarized affidavit or certificate) (manual p. 3)
teen.passengerLimit: Junior license: first 6 months one non-family passenger under 18; then three, unless ever partly or fully at fault in a crash or convicted of a driving violation; no limit when a parent, guardian, person in loco parentis or spouse 18 or older is in the car; never more than the seat belts (manual p. 3-4)
teen.phone: All drivers: Paul Miller's Law, hand-held devices banned while driving, even stopped in traffic or at a light (effective June 5, 2025; $50 fines from June 5, 2026). Texting ban also applies.

notes: Handbook checked: PA Driver's Manual PUB 95 (4-21), English, April 2021 edition, still the PDF linked from pa.gov on 2026-10-09. Printed page = PDF page - 4.
Knowledge test: 18 multiple-choice questions, 15 correct to pass (manual p. 5; online manual Testing page). One try per day; retake the next business day.
Test languages: the current online manual (Testing page) lists 30 languages, written and audio, on request. The 2021 PDF (p. 5) lists a shorter list of 18.
Supervising driver (manual p. 2-3): licensed driver 21 or older, or a licensed parent, guardian, person in loco parentis or spouse 18 or older, in the front seat.
School bus (manual p. 58): stop at least 10 feet away; failure brings a 60-day suspension, five points and a fine. Only exception: opposite side of a divided highway (reduce speed, use caution).

Move Over law (manual p. 59; formerly called Steer Clear): move to a lane not next to an emergency response area or disabled vehicle, or slow to at least 20 mph below the posted limit; 2 points; fines up to $500 / $1,000 / $2,000.
Under 18: 90-day suspension at 6 or more points or 26 mph or more over the limit (manual p. 4, 79).
Paul Miller's Law (hand-held ban, effective June 5, 2025; $50 fines from June 5, 2026) is newer than the 2021 manual; source: PennDOT newsroom and 75 Pa.C.S. 3316.1.
Learner's permit valid one year (manual p. 2-3).
